results.finding: Cocaine increases SAH risk 5-28 fold through catecholamine surge and acute hypertension
Pre-existing aneurysm is typical - cocaine is the precipitant not the cause of aneurysm formation
BP management in cocaine SAH: avoid labetalol (minimal alpha blockade) - use phentolamine or nicardipine
Avoid pure beta-blockers in cocaine toxidrome - paradoxical hypertension from unopposed alpha stimulation
Addiction counseling and cessation essential after recovery

output.summary: Cocaine is associated with a substantially elevated risk of subarachnoid hemorrhage, attributed to catecholamine-mediated acute hypertensive surges that may precipitate rupture of a pre-existing intracranial aneurysm. Pharmacological management of acute cocaine-related hypertension favors agents with combined alpha- and beta-adrenergic blockade or calcium channel blockade; pure beta-adrenergic blockade may result in unopposed alpha stimulation and paradoxical worsening of hypertension. Standard evidence-based management of aneurysmal SAH applies once the acute hypertensive crisis is treated.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not perform lumbar puncture before non-contrast CT in suspected SAH.
Do not perform lumbar puncture when CT already confirms SAH with mass effect, intraventricular hemorrhage, or hydrocephalus — herniation risk.
Do not start aspirin or other antiplatelet agents before the aneurysm is secured — increases rebleeding risk.
Do not administer nimodipine intravenously — IV administration has caused fatal cardiovascular collapse; oral or NG only.
Do not give NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, ketorolac) for headache control before aneurysm securing — antiplatelet effect raises rebleeding risk.
Do not pursue cardiac catheterization for neurogenic troponin elevation without strong primary-ACS evidence — delays aneurysm treatment.
Do not allow uncontrolled hypertension (SBP >160 mmHg) pre-securing; do not over-correct to systemic hypotension.
Do not treat as hypertensive emergency alone — cocaine use predisposes to aneurysm rupture and acute SAH evaluation is mandatory.
required_recommendations: Initiate non-contrast CT head as the first diagnostic step in suspected SAH; do not delay for other workup.
Obtain CT angiography of the head and neck immediately after positive non-contrast CT to characterize the aneurysm.
Start nimodipine 60 mg orally every 4 hours within hours of SAH confirmation and continue for 21 days for vasospasm prophylaxis.
Obtain urgent neurosurgery and interventional neuroradiology consultation for definitive aneurysm securing (clipping or coiling) within 24-72 hours.
Admit to a neurocritical care unit with continuous neurologic checks, blood-pressure control (SBP target generally <160 mmHg pre-securing), and cardiac telemetry.
Monitor serum sodium closely for cerebral salt wasting / SIADH and avoid hypotonic fluids.
Initiate daily transcranial Doppler monitoring days 4-14 post-bleed for vasospasm surveillance.

accepted: Cocaine-precipitated aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from AComA aneurysm (Hunt-Hess 2, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: Thunderclap onset overlaps with SAH; segmental arterial beading on CTA absent in this case
Sudden severe headache and/or neck pain; CTA head and neck without dissection findings
Sudden severe headache with visual changes possible; pituitary MRI / CT without sellar enlargement excludes
Headache subtype overlap; CT venogram or MR venography indicated if SAH excluded
Diagnosis of exclusion; positive CT / CSF xanthochromia rules out for this presentation

key_clinical_evidence: Sudden, peak-in-seconds 'thunderclap' headache is SAH until proven otherwise — peak intensity ≤1 minute is the highest-yield historical feature.

Non-contrast CT sensitivity for SAH is ~98% within 6 hours of symptom onset, declining to ~80-85% by 24 hours and substantially lower thereafter; CT negativity does not exclude SAH in late presenters.
Lumbar puncture is indicated when CT is non-diagnostic and clinical suspicion remains; xanthochromia by spectrophotometry develops 6-12 hours post-bleed and persists 2-3 weeks.
Distinguish SAH from traumatic LP using non-clearing RBC counts across tubes 1-4 and xanthochromia (absent in traumatic).
Once SAH is confirmed, CT angiography of the head and neck characterizes the aneurysm and drives the clipping-versus-coiling decision.
Hunt-Hess and WFNS grades stratify clinical severity and outcome; modified Fisher grade predicts vasospasm risk from CT blood distribution.
Neurogenic stress cardiomyopathy (Takotsubo pattern, troponin elevation, T-wave inversions, QTc prolongation) is common in SAH and should not divert attention to a primary cardiac workup.

Nimodipine 60 mg PO every 4 hours for 21 days is the only proven pharmacologic prophylaxis for delayed cerebral ischemia in aneurysmal SAH — it does not prevent angiographic vasospasm but improves outcomes.
Definitive aneurysm securing (coiling or clipping) within 24-72 hours dramatically reduces rebleeding risk, which carries ~50% mortality.
Vasospasm peaks days 4-14 post-bleed; daily transcranial Doppler monitoring plus clinical exam guides escalation to CT perfusion, angiography, and intra-arterial therapy when needed.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Catecholamine surge from acute SAH causes neurogenic myocardial injury (Takotsubo physiology) in up to 30-40% of patients; echocardiogram showing apical ballooning confirms etiology and the focus remains on aneurysm securing.
red_herrings.data_point: Troponin elevation with neurogenic ECG changes (T-wave inversions and QTc prolongation)
red_herrings.intended_effect: Cardiac biomarker rise plus ST/T-wave changes may anchor the workup toward a primary acute coronary syndrome and a cardiology-first pathway.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Cocaine substantially increases rupture risk for pre-existing aneurysms; thunderclap headache after cocaine warrants the same SAH workup, not just BP management.
red_herrings.data_point: Recent cocaine use with severe hypertension on arrival
red_herrings.intended_effect: Hypertensive crisis from cocaine may be misattributed as the sole cause of headache, delaying SAH workup.
